parts: Anything that aids you in doing work is an equipment. Electrical equipment needs electricity (toaster, mixie, immersion rod, iron, refrigerator, washing machine, geyser); non-electrical equipment is manually operated or uses another fuel (utensils, sewing machine, cooking stove, solar cooker). A 'grameen sheetal' is a wire-mesh cupboard covered with jute cloth (taat) whose ends dip in bowls of water so the cloth stays wet; it keeps food cool without electricity but is cheaper and cannot do all that a refrigerator can. Efficient use includes correct selection, operation and care.

Points to consider: (1) need-based (not because others have it or it is cheap), (2) saves time, money and energy (a pressure cooker saves time, fuel and supervision; a sharp knife saves energy), (3) easy to clean (stainless steel over iron; toaster with removable crumb tray), (4) safe (ISI mark guarantees safety of electrical goods; 3-pin plug and insulated cord; no exposed metal; no sharp edges or loose handles; guarantee of service: a promise that the manufacturer will repair free for a stated period, e.g. 5 years for refrigerators, 7 for fans; the guarantee card should be filled, signed and stamped), (5) cost (costlier equipment performs more functions but a simple model may suit your need), (6) after-sales service available locally. Standardised products meet minimum standards of safety, durability and performance.

Read and follow the instructions; check wires and plugs; remove the plug before cleaning; keep electrical equipment away from water taps; do not touch with wet hands; stop using equipment that gives even a light shock; keep wires out of the walking path; use proper fuses or an MCB (mini circuit breaker, which cuts off supply on overload, short circuit or sudden voltage rise); do not wear synthetic clothes in the kitchen (nylon melts and sticks to skin); use pans with bakelite or wooden handles and tongs or a napkin (never the pallu); clean equipment after every use; fill a kerosene stove only up to 2/3 and never refill while on; replace a cracked LPG tube, worn wires and a hard pressure-cooker gasket; turn off the LPG knob when not in use; store knives with the blade pointing down; keep the cooker vent pipe clean and wait for the hissing to stop before opening; no metal spoons or hard scrubbers for non-stick pans; oil sewing machines; use only microwave-proof containers in a microwave oven.

Fuel: clean burners, bring frozen food to room temperature, soak pulses and rice, use a pressure cooker (lower the flame after the first whistle) and separators, cover the pan, cool hot food before refrigerating and use a solar cooker. Electricity: avoid frequent fridge door opening, switch off lights and fans, use low-wattage tubelights and CFLs, minimise geyser, washing machine and mixer use, repair defects, use solar lantern, cooker and water heater, and use TVs and computers sparingly. Water: reuse clothes-washing water for mopping and vegetable-washing water for plants, use a bucket and mug instead of a shower or running tap, water plants and wash the car with a bucket rather than a pipe and do not let the water cooler overflow.
